sentences.show: She was aboard three sister ships. One crashed, one hit an iceberg, one hit a mine. She survived all three.
Her name was Violet Jessop, an ocean liner stewardess.
In 1911, she was working on the Olympic, the biggest liner in the world.
Leaving Southampton, it collided with a Royal Navy cruiser.
The hull was torn open. Nobody died.
Seven months later, Violet joined Olympic's new sister ship. Titanic.
On the night of 14 April 1912, it struck an iceberg.
She was ordered on deck, to show the passengers how to stay calm.
As lifeboat 16 was lowered, an officer handed her a baby.
She later said she heard the band playing a hymn. Nearer, My God, to Thee. Others swore they didn't.
The Carpathia picked them up. There, a woman snatched the baby from her, and ran off without a word.
In the First World War, Violet became a nurse, on the third sister. The hospital ship Britannic.
In November 1916, Britannic hit a German mine off Greece.
Lifeboats were sucked into the ship's spinning propellers. Hers was next.
She jumped into the sea, and hit her head badly. She survived that too.
Then she went back to sea, for another thirty years.
Violet Jessop died in 1971, aged 83. They called her Miss Unsinkable.
Three ships couldn't sink her. Don't let her story sink. Subscribe.
